paragraph.text: SkinSure — End-to-End Technical Write-Up
Overview & scope

SkinSure is a clinical decision-support prototype for skin-disease screening, built specifically for Fitzpatrick IV–VI skin tones (the project's stated target, underrepresented in most public dermatology datasets). It is explicitly
a diagnostic device — the product framing throughout the documentation is "a screening aid that says 'see a doctor' readily."

The system is a six-stage pipeline: image in → preprocessing → a 3-model deep learning ensemble → Grad-CAM explainability → an LLM-based clinical summarizer → deterministic severity triage → structured output out. A separate, parked track adds federated learning as an alternative training regime. A further, largely-planned track ("A0–A9", the Production Agent Engineering plan) covers observability, evals, guardrails and LLMOps for the agentic layer.

Numbers are quoted exactly as stated in those files — not rounded, softened, or reconciled across files where the files themselves flag unresolved discrepancies (these are called out explicitly in §9). A grid search over 1,033 weight vectors on the clean 565-set found an EfficientNet+Swin ("ES", dropping ConvNeXt) configuration reaching 99.19% melanoma sensitivity vs the shipped ECS's 97.58% — a 1.6pp gap on the single most safety-critical metric.

text.bold: This was tested for significance and did not survive

paragraph.text: : only 2 discordant images, McNemar exact p=0.50, Wilson 95% CIs overlap substantially (ECS [93.13,99.17]% vs ES [95.57,99.86]%). Key design decision: ranked-melanoma escalation (ADR-F4) — built, shipped OFF
While investigating F1, it was discovered that all three melanomas the ECS ensemble misses share one shape: melanoma ranks high but is

text.bold: no threshold adjustment of that rule can ever catch these cases

paragraph.text: — a structural blind spot invisible to melanoma-sensitivity metrics computed on argmax predictions. A new rule ("F4") was built that reads the full

paragraph.text: (i.i.d. pixel-level noise) posts the

Key design principle: "a derived figure needs its denominator" (PUBLISHABLE_FINDINGS F3)
A confirmed, reproduced defect:
originally passed

as a bare fraction ("Model agreement: 0.33"). In two independent live runs, the LLM inferred the wrong denominator — "the two models agree at only 0.33" when actually 1 of 3 agreed, and "the two models agree completely" when 3 of 3 did. Fixed by stating the count explicitly ("1 of 3 models agree with the primary label (score 0.33, low tier)"), after which the next run reported correctly. Documented as a general design rule for any LLM-in-the-loop clinical system: a derived number handed to a model needs its denominator stated, or the model will invent one, and the invented value lands in patient-facing text.

Key design decision, stated as an explicit rule of thumb (A9)
The plan's "cheapest correct component wins" framework,

text.bold: applied retroactively to justify choices already made

paragraph.text: in Stages 2–5: lesion classification uses classic ML (fixed label set, calibratable, CPU-cheap) rather than an LLM/VLM; severity triage uses deterministic rules (auditable, injection-immune) rather than an LLM; the clinical summary uses prompting (language generation over already-structured facts, no external knowledge needed) rather than RAG or fine-tuning. Fine-tuning is explicitly rejected for any current component: "no high-volume, high-quality target data; prompting + guards meets the gates."
Gaps/limitations

text.bold: A2 through A9 are plans, not code.

paragraph.text: No replay traces exist, no failure taxonomy has been written, no ship gates are enforced in CI, no guardrail/permission layer wraps the summarizer, no fallback/circuit-breaker exists, no red-teaming has been run, no data-governance documents (
) exist, and no production deployment exists for A8 to monitor.
The plan itself flags several of its own prior estimates as

: an original ~2.3s Grad-CAM latency estimate (from a single synthetic image) was revised to 2.6–15.7s after real-photo testing; an original $0.01 cost-per-query gate was revised down after the real measured ~$0.0005/call baseline showed ~14× slack.
The plan is explicit that none of its ship-gate thresholds are clinical standards — "engineering starting points" requiring clinician review before any real-patient use, which has not occurred.

Model generation integrity (v1 vs v2), the other major cross-cutting thread
As detailed in Stage 2, all three original ("v1") checkpoints

text.bold: failed to reproduce their own stored accuracy

paragraph.text: when reloaded and re-scored — the project's single largest data-integrity finding, which motivated a full retrain ("v2") with an explicit save-then-verify gate (bit-identical tensor reload + re-score within 1e-9 of the stored metric). The v1 checkpoints and an older bare-state-dict set (~479MB) were deleted 2026-11-02 and are not recoverable from git.

text.bold: Generations must never be mixed across backbones

paragraph.text: — enforced by the app's checkpoint loader, which refuses to load a mixed set rather than silently combining a v1 and two v2 checkpoints.

A documented, load-bearing convention repeated verbatim across CLAUDE.md and PUBLISHABLE_FINDINGS.md: three test sets exist (997-image FL split, 727-image contaminated paper set, 565-image de-duplicated clean set) and

text.bold: must never be compared with each other

paragraph.text: — every figure in this write-up that cites an accuracy or sensitivity number is attributed to its specific basis for this reason.

The honest overall status, in one paragraph
The

text.bold: core screening pipeline is built, measured, and internally self-consistent

paragraph.text: : three independently retrained and integrity-verified model checkpoints, a documented and tested safety-override layer that the LLM cannot bypass, a measured (not assumed) explainability faithfulness result, and two formally resolved preprocessing A/B experiments with opposite outcomes (one harmful, one inert) that together produced a reusable finding about what separates them. The

text.bold: surrounding production infrastructure — deployment, monitoring, guardrails, security testing, data governance, and three of six planned agents — is either partially built (tracing) or entirely unbuilt (everything else in the A2–A9 track, containerization, CI/CD, and cloud hosting)

paragraph.text: . The project's own documentation is unusually candid about this distinction throughout, consistently separating "measured" from "planned" and "CONFIRMED" from "PROVISIONAL" rather than blending the two.
